items.context: Round 1 settled on inline full-width images with click-to-lightbox (d2=A). The codebase currently has no lightbox component. We need to decide how to implement this.

options.label: Simple custom modal overlay using existing Dialog/overlay patterns
options.rationale: The codebase already uses absolute overlays (z-40 for detail pages) and Tailwind utilities. A lightweight custom lightbox (dark backdrop + centered image + close button) avoids adding a dependency and stays consistent with the existing UI. Recommended because the swarm-manager UI is intentionally dependency-light.

options.label: Use a lightweight lightbox library (e.g., yet-another-react-lightbox)
options.rationale: Gets pinch-to-zoom, swipe gestures, and keyboard navigation out of the box. Adds ~15KB but saves implementation time if attachment-heavy usage is expected.

options.label: Skip lightbox entirely — inline full-width is sufficient for now
options.rationale: Simplest approach. Users can right-click to open images in new tab for full resolution. Reduces scope but slightly lower UX quality.

items.topic: selectionToNodeId handling for captures (not graph nodes)
items.context: All existing detail pages call selectionToNodeId() to highlight the corresponding graph node. Captures are NOT graph nodes (out of scope per plan). The function currently returns null for unknown entity types via the default case. We need to decide how the detail page handles this.

options.label: Return null from selectionToNodeId for captures; detail page skips node highlighting
options.rationale: The existing default case already returns null. CaptureDetailsPage simply won't call any node-highlight logic. No code change needed in selectionToNodeId. Cleanest approach since captures aren't graph nodes.

options.label: Add explicit 'capture' case to selectionToNodeId returning null
options.rationale: Makes the intent explicit in the switch statement. Slightly more readable but functionally identical to option A. Minor code change.

items.notes: Pre-selected: the default case already handles this correctly. No action needed.

items.context: The capture store already fetches and caches the full captures list. captureService.get(id) also exists for single-capture fetching. The question is whether the detail page should read from the store (already loaded) or make a fresh API call via useQuery.

options.label: Read from capture store first, fall back to API fetch
options.rationale: Since CapturesTab already loads captures into the store, the detail page can read from store for instant rendering. If missing (deep-link with empty store), fall back to captureService.get(id). Best perceived performance for the common click-through case.

options.label: Always use useQuery with captureService.get(id)
options.rationale: Consistent with other detail pages (BacklogDetailsPage, InitiativeDetailsPage all use useQuery). Simpler code, but adds a redundant API call when navigating from sidebar since data is already in the store.

items.context: Round 1 settled on extracting a shared triage component from CaptureCard (d3=A). CaptureCard currently handles: per-item accept/edit/dismiss buttons, 'accept all' batch action, auto-dismiss on completion, retry classification, and delete. The detail page needs all of these. The question is extraction granularity.

options.label: Extract a CaptureTriage component covering suggestion list + actions
options.rationale: Single component that renders the classified items list with accept/edit/dismiss per item, plus 'accept all'. CaptureCard and CaptureDetailsPage both use it. Keeps delete/retry/dismiss-capture as parent-level actions since they differ by context. Good balance of reuse vs. flexibility.

options.label: Extract individual action button components only
options.rationale: Smaller extraction — shared AcceptButton, DismissButton, EditButton. Each parent composes its own layout. More flexible but more assembly work in each consumer.

items.text: captureService.get(id) already exists in capture-service.ts (line 68) and returns a fully mapped Capture object. The API endpoint GET /api/v1/captures/{id} is confirmed working via the CLI. No backend work needed.
